newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BOSTON'S MO VAUGHN TO UNDERGO KNEE SURGERY.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BOSTON'S MO VAUGHN TO UNDERGO KNEE SURGERY.

text.p: Boston Red Sox first baseman Mo Vaughn was scheduled to undergo arthroscopic surgery on his ailing left knee Tuesday and will miss two to six weeks, the team announced Monday.
Vaughn, the 1995 American League Most Valuable Player, was examined Monday by team physician Dr. Arthur Pappas, who determined surgery was needed to repair torn cartilage.
"Different people respond differently. I'll be able to give a better estimate once I give a look inside his knee tomorrow," Pappas said of Vaughn's timetable for returning to the Red Sox lineup.
"It's torn sufficiently. There are people, though, who return in three weeks and others who return in six weeks. It perhaps could be a little longer than shorter," Pappas predicted.

Vaughn's knee locked up on him in Wednesday's 10-1 rout of Baltimore. He was able to return to the lineup, but the knee locked up on him again after he slid into home plate in the third inning of Sunday night's 10-1 romp over the Mets.
"When I saw him this morning, his knee remained locked," Pappas said.

The 29-year-old slugger, Boston's most dangerous hitter, is batting .335 with 20 homers and 45 RBI in 65 games. He ranks eighth in the American League in hitting, fourth in homers and sixth in slugging percentage.
